previous_statement: Under the root antecedent and the choices in 1.1, rho+epsilon_{A_R}<=(C_cross^0+1)*t<=a_merge. Hence lem-extcb-four-corner-merge, applied to the supplied amplified four-corner datum, yields a bijective v:B_U oplus B_V->A_R that is an extended delta-isomorphism for delta:=C_merge*(rho+epsilon_{A_R}). As delta is a nonnegative defect parameter, delta<=abs(C_merge)*(rho+epsilon_{A_R})<=K*t<=D_3*t. By def-extended-delta-inclusion, replacing a nonnegative defect bound by a larger one only relaxes every amplified homomorphism-error and two-sided norm inequality, while bijectivity is unchanged; therefore v is an extended D_3*t-isomorphism.
new_statement: The merge conclusion does not follow from the root antecedent.  The external lem-extcb-four-corner-merge requires, in addition to def-four-corner-merging-datum and the smallness inequality from 1.2, that all four fixed level-one corner maps be bijective.  Def-four-corner-merging-datum and the root antecedent contain no such condition.  This is a substantive omission: there are exact common-defect-zero four-corner data with non-surjective diagonal corner maps and with source and target of different finite dimensions, so no bijective assembled map can exist.  Thus the previous application of lem-extcb-four-corner-merge is invalid; to recover it, the root antecedent must explicitly require the four level-one corner maps to be bijective (after which 1.2 supplies its remaining smallness hypothesis).
